narrative:
The machine learning model predicted a 50% chance that you would fail the bar exam, which is a significant concern for your application to law school. This prediction played a crucial role in the decision to deny your admission. 

The most influential factor in this prediction was your Year 3 academic performance, which placed you in a lower decile compared to the average of accepted students. While your Year 1 grades were on par with those of successful applicants, your Year 3 performance was notably below average, suggesting a decline in your academic trajectory. This decline raises concerns about your preparedness for the rigorous demands of law school and the bar exam.

Additionally, your decision to work part-time while studying may have contributed to the prediction. Most accepted students are able to commit to full-time studies, which likely enhances their focus and performance. This difference in study commitment could impact your ability to prepare adequately for the bar exam.

Lastly, your undergraduate GPA, while respectable, was slightly below the average of those who were accepted. This further compounded the concerns about your overall academic readiness.

Given these factors, it would be beneficial for you to focus on improving your academic performance, particularly in your final year, and consider dedicating more time to your studies. Strengthening your application with a higher GPA and demonstrating a commitment to full-time study could enhance your chances of success in future applications.
